1308468.label: House — whole-home service

rate_periods.note: The earliest bill on hand: the first day billed by the 2025-09-25..10-27 cycle. The true effective date is earlier and unknown, so nothing before this can be priced.

An interim rate, collected subject to refund while the PSC case was open. It was superseded on 2026-01-29 and the difference came back as the `2025-Rate Refund Credit` on the 2026-04-30 bill (-$25.52 house, -$1.83 barn). That credit sits in an `Other Charges` block BELOW `Total Current Charges`, so it is not part of what verify-bill reconciles -- it is a separate line on the amount due.

The DSM rate changed alone, so no date is printed — the bill shows only a split of 410 of 2,424 kWh at the old rate over the 2026-03-26..04-28 cycle. The evidence does not pin a single day: day-proration brackets it at 2026-03-31..04-02, and allocating by the barn's actual metered usage points nearer 2026-04-04. 04-01 is used as the administratively likely date. The whole question is worth under $0.05 on a monthly bill at the $0.00054/kWh delta, which is why it is not chased further.

1308468.notes: Residential Electric Service. Flat energy charge -- no tiers, no seasonal split, no time-of-use, across all ten bills. The $0.30 home energy assistance charge is a flat monthly amount and is the only untaxed line.

1326254.notes: General Service Single Phase -- a COMMERCIAL schedule, on its own account. Pays both the 3% school tax and 6% Kentucky sales tax, and carries a demand (kW) register that the bill prints as `Information Only` and does NOT bill. No home energy assistance charge. Nothing sub-meters the barn, so this tariff is only ever priced against the meter series.

_readme: LG&E tariff parameters, transcribed from the bills in data/bills/ (which are NOT
committed -- they are account documents). `energycap verify-bill` prices a billing
cycle from this file and compares the result to what LG&E actually charged.
The utility ACCOUNT NUMBERS are deliberately left empty: this repository is public, and
the account number is the one identifier here that is neither needed to price a cycle nor
already published elsewhere in the repo (the meter ids are, in channel_map.json). Fill
them in locally if you want verify-bill to echo them back; nothing depends on them. Same
reasoning as the phone number in docs/lge-greenbutton.md.
This file is HAND-MAINTAINED. Add a block to `billing_cycles` each month from the new
bill; add to `rate_periods` only when the basic/energy/DSM rate itself changes.
tests/test_tariff.py replays every cycle here and requires all of them to reproduce
`billed_total` to the cent, so a transcription slip fails the suite rather than
quietly biasing the answer.
The order of operations is not obvious and is not the same on both schedules -- see
`rider_base_includes_fuel_adjustment` and `rider_base_deduction_per_kwh` below, and
the docstring in src/energy_capture/tariff.py.
The two services are on DIFFERENT rate schedules and DIFFERENT accounts. The house is
residential and exempt from the 6% Kentucky sales tax as the customer's primary
residence; the barn is billed as General Service and pays it. Never price one with the
other's tariff.

_field_notes.rate_periods: The tariff proper: open-ended, changes only when the PSC approves a new rate. `effective_from` is a LOCAL date, inclusive, and is the first day BILLED at that rate (so it is one day after the read date when a change lands on a cycle boundary). A cycle spanning a change is split across two printed lines; the 2026-01-01 boundary was solved directly from the barn's 15-minute series and agrees with the bill exactly.
_field_notes.billing_cycles: What LG&E actually charged, one block per bill. The fuel adjustment and the three percentage riders are RESET EVERY MONTH by the utility and cannot be predicted -- the 10 months here span 0.00048 to 0.01063 $/kWh on the fuel adjustment alone, a 22x range. So this list is history, not a forecast: pricing a cycle that has no block here uses the most recent one and says the rider figures are ESTIMATED.
_field_notes.rider_base_includes_fuel_adjustment: Whether the fuel adjustment is inside the base the percentage riders apply to. TRUE on Residential, FALSE on General Service. Verified against all 20 bills.
_field_notes.rider_base_deduction_per_kwh: General Service subtracts a flat per-kWh amount from the rider base -- the bill prints it as e.g. `(0.73% x ($157.59 - $24.94))`. $0.0286/kWh reproduces the subtrahend to the cent on all ten barn bills. Zero on Residential.
_field_notes.cycle_end: `cycle_start` and `cycle_end` are the two meter READ dates exactly as the bill prints them. The days actually billed are (cycle_start, cycle_end] -- the previous read date's usage belongs to the previous cycle, the current read date's usage to this one. MEASURED, not assumed: over the barn's eight fully covered cycles the mean absolute error against billed kWh is 3.67% treating the read date as exclusive and 0.16% on this convention, and the house's three agree (0.56% -> 0.05%). The day COUNT is identical either way, so a bill still reconciles on the wrong convention and only the kWh move -- see energy_capture.tariff.billing_days.
_field_notes.school_tax_pct: Applied to (total electric charges - home energy assistance charge). The HEA charge is the one line that is never taxed.
_field_notes.sales_tax_pct: Kentucky sales tax, applied to (total electric charges + school tax) -- it is levied on top of the school tax, not alongside it. 0 for the house: residential service at the customer's declared primary residence is exempt.
